note: First reproducible model-side inference reference for the V4-clean adapter on the HF/PEFT backend, local development machine. Frozen: future runs get their own experiment id.
objective: Model-side generation latency of the V4 classifier, measured under a fixed, reproducible protocol (Issue #9).

timing.out_of_scope_handling: timed and reported separately as pipeline stages; never pooled into the primary metric
timing.synchronization: torch.cuda.synchronize() immediately before starting and immediately after stopping the generate() timer, so completed GPU work is measured rather than submitted work
timing.not_measured: API latency, proxy overhead and end-to-end gateway latency. Those belong to Issue #18. The D3 budget of end-to-end P95 <= 200 ms is not evaluated here.

selection.order: file order of the eval split (as generated by parse_dataset_v4.py); labels are interleaved, not grouped
selection.seed_scope: warm-up request selection only; request order is not shuffled

populations.model_load: load_model() in a fresh process — 1 sample per run

first_inference.description: first generate() in a fresh process (cold start)

steady_state.description: the measurement set — the only population in the reported latency statistics
steady_state.note: The cold-start and warm-up rows are members of the split and are therefore executed again inside this pass. Their cold/warm samples stay in their own populations; the steady sample of the same row is a separate, later observation. Greedy decoding is deterministic, so re-running a row cannot change its decision.

runs.process_model: one fresh OS process per run; model loaded once per process
runs.reuse: the loaded model is reused for every request in a run

generation.unchanged: model, adapter, prompt, parsing, generation parameters and quantization are exactly those of the V4 runtime configuration (D27). Nothing was tuned for this benchmark.

statistics.outlier_policy: no outlier removal; extreme samples are characterized
statistics.aggregation_across_runs: Two views, both reported. POOLED: every steady sample from every run in one distribution — the headline figure. PER-RUN: each run's own statistics, plus their min/median/max/mean/stdev/range, which is the run-to-run variation.
statistics.headline: pooled steady-state generate() P95

quality.metrics: E5 binary metrics via test_model.score_binary (BLOCK positive)
quality.purpose: a latency result is only meaningful next to the quality produced at that latency
